name: Daikanyama
tagline: Shibuya in 3 minutes and Shinjuku in 13 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥150,000 to ¥160,000.
summary: The station is in Shibuya City, where Tokyu run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 26 minutes to Otemachi, 13 minutes to Shinjuku, 3 minutes to Shibuya and 29 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. The station stands 24.7 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 23.5 m. The land around the station rises and falls sharply.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 24.7 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 9.7 m to 33.2 m, a difference of 23.5 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 1 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is less than 0.5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 18 clinics and 9 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 東京共済病院, about 13 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is アイシークリニック渋谷院, about 15 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyu Toyoko Line.
congestion: Tokyu Toyoko Line runs at 124% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 祐天寺→中目黒, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 1K ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. 1LDK ¥270,000 to ¥280,000 and 2LDK ¥390,000 to ¥400,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the highest in the 23 wards. a small projected flood depth pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station and a climb from the station to much of the housing holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Ebisu; for quiet, Daikanyama.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Daikanyama. Ebisu has 4 lines that Daikanyama does not. With more lines, Ebisu is the better connected of the two. To Shinagawa, for instance, Ebisu is 10 minutes quicker. On quiet, though, Daikanyama comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Naka-Meguro; for how easy the shopping is, Daikanyama.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Daikanyama. Naka-Meguro also has the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line, which Daikanyama does not. With more lines, Naka-Meguro is the better connected of the two. To Toranomon, for instance, Naka-Meguro is 6 minutes quicker. A one-room flat also costs about ¥26,000 less at Naka-Meguro. On how easy the shopping is, though, Daikanyama comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station rises and falls sharply, and living above or below the slope changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 13 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyu Toyoko Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are very lightly loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: Whether a flat faces the road changes what you hear indoors.
